newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania central bank sees currency reserves up.
newsitem.headline: Romania central bank sees currency reserves up.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu on Monday forecast a sharp increase in the BNR's foreign exchange reserves and further moves towards a more flexible but cautious monetary policy.
Isarescu's predictions came on the eve of an International Monetary Fund board meeting to discuss fresh loans for Romania.

"The BNR's reserves are seen rising to $1.4-$1.5 billion early in May and reach about $2.0 billion in June or July, if one considers the amounts we expect to get from the IMF and the European Union as well as our purchases from the local foreign exchange market," Isarescu told a news conference.
He predicted a sharp rise in the BNR's foreign exchange reserves from a current $1.1 billion, also spawned by cash inflows from exports and higher direct and portfolio investments in Romania.

Romania hopes to get about $400 million in Fund loans this year as well as $70 million Ecus from the EU. The expected IMF credits, designed to underpin faster market reforms, would be disbursed in five tranches of $80 million.
Isarescu said the IMF board would discuss resuming loans to Romania on Tuesday, one day earlier than previously announced.
Earlier this month the IMF chief negotiator for Romania said the country's chances to secure credits were "very good" and that the government was on track with promised reforms.

Romania's new centrist coalition government, which ousted leftists in last November's elections, pledged to step up market reforms, which started with tougher monetary policy followed by food and fuel price liberalisation.
The IMF suspended loans to Romania in 1996 over the former government's delaying reforms and curbing currency markets.
Isarescu also said the BNR would set a fixed annual Lombard rate of 200 percent this week, lower than 256 previously.

The Lombard rate, charged on overdraft credits, was allowed to float in line with the auctioned rates earlier this year, which pushed it to an all-time high of 682.4 percent in February before a gradual slip to 256 percent last week.
Isarescu said the Lombard rate would be periodically adjusted to monetary policy goals. "It is essential that our monetary policy should remain tight."
Monthly inflation hit an all-time high of 30.7 percent in March after the price liberalisation, pushing the first quarter inflation figure to 76.5 percent.

The BNR also planned to introduce open-market operations, lending flexibility to the monetary policy. "We will cancel our auction for refinancing credits this Thursday and we might sterilise part of the funds offered through other refinancing facilities," Isarescu said.

The BNR had provided leu liquidity through purchases of "excess" dollars from the market to prevent a sharp firming of the local leu currency in the past month, Isarescu said. "We have to support the greenback having in mind the large inflows of hard currency on our market".
The leu has been fairly stable over the past weeks at about 7,050/100 to the dollar, in a smooth recover after a plunge to 9,000 in mid-February from about 4,100 in the New Year.
